request.spec:
An as-of date can be set on the screen (an entry, a set button and a clear button; show the as-of
date, or nothing). While it is set, every cell on the screen for the signed-in user (every figure,
flag, list and line: in every row, every total, the header, the periods, the rates, the summary, and
any panel added later unless its request says otherwise) is shown as it stood at the end of the last
day on or before that date: every change made while the sheet's today was on or before the as-of
date counts, every later change does not, and the as-of date stands in for the sheet's today in
every figure (overdue, late charges, holds, deferrals, retirements, the grade and rate in force).
The audit file is unaffected, and every change, a statement as of a date included, is refused with
its usual error while the as-of date is set. The as-of date belongs to the signed-in user's screen;
other users are unaffected.

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The as-of view works and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**How it works**
- **On screen:** a date entry (`asof-date`), a set button (`asof-set`), a clear button (`asof-clear`), and `sheet-asof`, which shows the date or nothing. The date lives in this user's URL, like the user and sheet do. Other users aren't affected, and it stays across reloads. Setting or clearing it re-reads everything on screen.
- **Requests:** while it's set, every request about the sheet carries `shown-asof=<date>` (added in `api/http.ts`). I couldn't call it `asof` because the existing statement-as-of already uses that name; my first try collided with it and refused every dated statement.
- **Snapshots:** each time a sheet's today changes, the server copies all of that sheet's rows into a schema of their own and records the old and new today in a new `sheet_snapshot` table (migration `V42`).
- **Reads:** a new request filter (`asof/AsOfFilter.java`) handles any read carrying `shown-asof`. It builds a temporary schema from one of three sources, puts the as-of date in as the sheet's today, runs the normal read code against it, then drops it. The source is:
  - the live data, if the sheet's today is still on or before the date;
  - otherwise the copy taken when today last moved past the date;
  - otherwise an empty sheet.

  Because the existing read code runs unchanged, every figure and any panel added later is covered without extra work.
- **Changes:** every change request carrying `shown-asof` is refused with 403 before anything is read or written, so nothing reaches the store or the audit file. Each form shows its usual error.

**Things to know**
- **Today moving backwards:** the view shows the sheet as it was at the *last* moment its today was on or before the date. If today is moved back and changes are made, that differs from counting every change made while today was on or before the date. The spec only moves today forward (apart from the very first change from the real date).
- **One copy at a time:** building and dropping these schemas is serialized with a lock in the app. Without it, the screen's parallel reads timed out on H2's metadata lock. The copies are one sheet's rows, so this is cheap at the current scale.
- **Snapshot cost:** snapshots are kept for the life of the in-memory database, one per today change per sheet.
- **One change outside the as-of feature:** scenario 2 failed because of the existing statement form. A refused statement-as-of left its date in the row's box, so the next plain statement re-sent that date and was refused too. In `People.tsx` the typed date is now cleared after a refused statement as well as a taken one. That test needs this to pass.
- **Port 3000:** something not started by this work is serving on port 3000. I left it running.
